text: This package loads data for react-window lists and grids as the user scrolls. It can be used as a hook or as a component. Version 2 of this package is for use with version 2 of react-window. Documentation for version 1 can be found here. Installation Begin by installing the library from NPM: npm install react-window-infinite-loader TypeScript definitions are included within the published dist folder. Support Here are some ways to support this project: Become a GitHub sponsor Buy me a coffee

headings.title: children
headings.text: children: (params: { onRowsRendered: OnRowsRendered; }) => ReactNode Render prop that receives an onRowsRendered callback to pass to a List.

headings.title: isRowLoaded
headings.text: isRowLoaded: (index: number) => boolean Function responsible for tracking the loaded state of each item.

headings.title: loadMoreRows
headings.text:
loadMoreRows: (startIndex: number, stopIndex: number) => Promise<void> Callback to be invoked when more rows must be loaded.
It should return a Promise that is resolved once all data has finished loading.

headings.title: rowCount
headings.text: rowCount: number Number of rows in list; can be arbitrary high number if actual number is unknown.

headings.title: minimumBatchSize
headings.text:
minimumBatchSize?: number Minimum number of rows to be loaded at a time; defaults to 10.
This property can be used to batch requests to reduce HTTP requests.

headings.title: threshold
headings.text:
threshold?: number Threshold at which to pre-fetch data; defaults to 15.
A threshold of 15 means that data will start loading when a user scrolls within 15 rows.
 The useInfiniteLoader hook accepts the same parameters, except for children.

text: Loads rows as they are scrolled into view; a render prop alternative to the useInfiniteLoader hook.
title: InfiniteLoader component props
useInfiniteLoader

headings.title: Parameters
headings.text: Parameters isRowLoaded : (index: number) => boolean Function responsible for tracking the loaded state of each row. loadMoreRows : (startIndex: number, stopIndex: number) => Promise<void> Callback to be invoked when more rows must be loaded. It should return a Promise that is resolved once all data has finished loading. Rows are not requested again while a request for them is in progress. Once the Promise settles, rows that are still not loaded (e.g. because the request failed) will be requested again the next time they are rendered. Errors should be handled within loadMoreRows. minimumBatchSize ?: number = 10 Minimum number of rows to be loaded at a time. This can be used to batch requests to reduce HTTP requests. rowCount : number Number of rows in the list; can be an arbitrarily high number if the actual number is unknown. threshold ?: number = 15 Threshold at which to pre-fetch data. A threshold of 15 means that data will start loading when a user scrolls within 15 rows.

text: GitHub is the easiest place to look for help, but it's probably not the fastest. This project is maintained by a single developer so there is limited bandwidth for answering questions. I recommend asking questions on Stack Overflow or Reddit to start with. Both sites have active communities who often respond quickly. If you don't find an answer there you can try opening a GitHub issue- but please take a moment first to see if your question has has already been answered before opening a new one.
